items.q: A list has its 5th member equal to (2 + 4/n) divided by 2. Find the largest value the members of that list can take.
items.s: The members are largest when n is smallest, at n = 1, giving (2 + 4)/2 = 3.

items.q: Find the limit of the list whose 5th member is (6n + 11) divided by (5n + 9).
items.s: Dividing every term by n leaves 6/5, so the limit is 1.2.

items.q: Find the limit of the list whose 2nd member is 2 divided by (n + 2).
items.s: The denominator grows without bound while the top stays fixed, so the members approach 0.

items.q: Find the limit of (x^2 - 4)/(x - 2) as x tends to 2.
items.s: Factorising gives x + 2, so as x tends to 2 the value tends to 4.

items.q: A map takes the value 2 for x greater than zero and the value 0 for x less than zero. Find the approach value as x comes towards zero from above.
items.s: For inputs greater than zero the output is constantly 2, so the approach value from above is 2.

items.q: Find the derivative of y = 2x^2 + 4x at x = 3 from the definition as a limit of a ratio of changes.
items.s: The difference quotient simplifies to 4x + 4 with a remainder that vanishes, so at x = 3 the value is 16.

items.q: A stretch of length 1 is split into 8 equal pieces. State the mesh of that split.
items.s: The pieces all have width 1/8, and the mesh is the widest width, which is 0.125.

items.q: A set consists of all numbers of the form 2/(n + 29) where n runs through the counting numbers. Find its infimum.
items.s: The largest denominator gives the smallest member, and as n grows without bound the members approach zero, so the greatest lower bound is 0 = 0.0667.

items.q: Find the supremum of the set of all x satisfying 3 < x < 7.
items.s: The members come arbitrarily close to 7 from below without reaching it, so the least upper bound is 3.

items.q: Using the triangle inequality, state the smallest number you can guarantee is at least as large as the size of x + y when the size of x is 3 and the size of y is 8.
items.s: The triangle inequality gives the size of the sum no more than the total of the separate sizes, which is 3 + 8 = 11.

items.q: Find the least counting number n for which n times 0.5 exceeds 3.
items.s: The inequality needs n greater than 3/0.5 = 6, so the least counting number that works is 7.

items.q: A list has its 2nd member equal to 1 - 1/4^n. State 1 if the list never decreases and 0 if it does.
items.s: As n grows the subtracted amount shrinks, so the members grow towards one and never decrease, recorded as 1.

items.q: A list converges to 4. Find the limit of the list obtained by keeping only the members in even positions.
items.s: Any part built by keeping members in their original order converges to the same value, so the limit stays 4.

items.q: A list has its 2nd member equal to 3. State 1 if the list satisfies the condition that its members eventually lie arbitrarily close to one another and 0 if it does not.
items.s: A list whose members are all equal certainly satisfies that condition, recorded as 1.

items.q: Find the limit of the list whose 3rd member is the square root of (n^2 + 8n) minus n.
items.s: Rationalising gives 8n divided by the square root of (n^2 + 8n) plus n, which tends to 8/2, that is 4.

items.q: Find the limit of the list whose 5th member is 4 divided by n multiplied by the sine of n.
items.s: The sine never exceeds one in size, so the members are trapped between plus and minus 4/n, both of which approach 0; the limit is therefore 0.

items.q: Find the limit of the list whose 3rd member is (1/2)^n.
items.s: The ratio 1/2 is less than one in size, so powers of it approach 0.

items.q: Find the sum of the endless total 1 + 1/3 + 1/3^2 + ... with common ratio 1/3.
items.s: The sum is the first term divided by one minus the ratio, that is 1/(1 - 1/3) = 1.5.

items.q: Find the sum of the first 10 members of the endless total 1 + 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + ...
items.s: The sum of the first 10 members is 2 minus the remainder after 10 terms, which is 10 to four decimal places.

items.q: The members of an endless total of positive numbers satisfy the condition that the ratio of successive members tends to 1/5. State the limit of that ratio.
items.s: The ratio tends to 1/5 = 0.2, which is less than one, so the total converges.

items.q: State 1 if the endless total of the reciprocals of the counting numbers settles to a finite value and 0 if it does not.
items.s: The running totals of the reciprocals of the counting numbers grow without bound, so the total does not settle, recorded as 0.

items.q: For which values of p does the endless total of 1/n^p settle to a finite value? State the smallest counting number p that you know certainly works.
items.s: The total settles for every p greater than one, and it fails at p = 1, so the smallest counting number that certainly works is 2.

items.q: A map is given by a polynomial of degree 3 on the whole line. State 1 if it is continuous at every input and 0 if it is not.
items.s: Every polynomial is continuous at every input, so the answer is 1.

items.q: Find the limit of sin(5x)/x as x tends to zero.
items.s: Since sin(u)/u tends to one, the quotient tends to 5, that is 5.

items.q: A continuous map takes the value -1 at one place and the value 2 at another. State the number whose existence between those two places is guaranteed by the intermediate value property.
items.s: A continuous map takes every value between -1 and 2, and zero lies between them, so a place where the output is 0 is guaranteed.

items.q: A continuous map on the closed stretch from 0 to 2 has its largest output equal to 9. State the largest output of the map on that stretch.
items.s: The extreme value property guarantees that the largest output is actually attained, and it is given as 9.

items.q: A continuous map on a closed stretch has outputs never below 3 and never above 2. State the smallest number you can guarantee is at least as large as every output of the map there.
items.s: Every output lies between 3 and 2, so 2 is at least as large as every output = 5.

items.q: A continuous map takes a negative value at one place and a positive value at another. State the least number of places between them where the output is zero that the sign change criterion guarantees.
items.s: The sign change criterion guarantees at least one such place, recorded as 1.

items.q: Differentiate y = 3x^3 from first principles and state the value of the derivative at x = 3.
items.s: The difference quotient simplifies to 3nx^2 with a remainder that vanishes, so at x = 3 the value is 81.

items.q: Differentiate y = 2/x from first principles and state the value of the derivative at x = 4.
items.s: The difference quotient tends to minus 2 divided by x squared, so at x = 4 the value is -0.125.

items.q: Differentiate y equal to the square root of x from first principles and state the value of the derivative at x = 1.
items.s: The derivative is one divided by twice the square root of x, so at x = 1 it is 0.5.

items.q: A map has a limit of the ratio of changes at a stated place. State 1 if the map must be continuous there and 0 if it need not be.
items.s: Having a limit of that ratio at a place forces continuity there, so the answer is 1.

items.q: A map takes the value 4 at x = 4 and the value -1 at x = 7. Find the average slope over that stretch.
items.s: The average slope is the change in output divided by the change in input, that is (-1 - 4)/3 = -1.67.

items.q: A map equals zero at x = 2 and at x = 2. Find the place inside the stretch where the guarantee of Rolle applies forces the touching slope to be zero, for the quadratic passing through both.
items.s: The place is halfway between 2 and 2, that is 2.

items.q: A differentiable map has the same value at x = 0 and at x = 2. State the least number of places inside the stretch where the touching slope is zero that the guarantee forces.
items.s: The guarantee forces at least one such place inside the stretch, recorded as 1.

items.q: Write the expansion of e^(3x) about zero as far as the term in x^3. State the coefficient of that term.
items.s: The coefficient is 3^3 divided by 3 factorial, which is 0.1667.

items.q: A differentiable map has a positive touching slope at every place of a stretch. State 1 if the map must rise across the stretch and 0 if it need not.
items.s: A positive touching slope throughout a stretch forces the map to rise across it, so the answer is 1.

items.q: The expansion of a map about zero is stopped after the term in x^2. State the power of x with which the remainder term begins, for a map whose derivatives of all orders exist.
items.s: Stopping after the term in x^2 leaves a remainder beginning with the power x^3.

items.q: For the map taking x to x^2 on the stretch from 0 to 3, split the stretch into 2 equal pieces and use the largest output on each piece. Find the resulting upper total.
items.s: The largest output on each piece is at its right end, and summing gives 16.88.

items.q: For the map taking x to x^2 on the stretch from 0 to 2, split the stretch into 2 equal pieces and use the smallest output on each piece. Find the resulting lower total.
items.s: The smallest output on each piece is at its left end, and summing gives 1.

items.q: For the map taking x to x^2 on the stretch from 0 to 3 split into 5 equal pieces, find the gap between the upper total and the lower total.
items.s: The two totals differ only in the last piece, and the gap is 3^2 times the width 0.6, giving 5.4.

items.q: A map never decreases on the closed stretch from 0 to 2. State 1 if it can certainly be integrated there and 0 if it cannot.
items.s: A map that never decreases on a closed stretch can always be integrated there, so the answer is 1.

items.q: The 2nd member of a family of maps takes x to x/(n + 2). Find the value the outputs settle on at x = 4.
items.s: With x fixed the denominator grows without bound, so the outputs settle on 0.

items.q: On the stretch from 0 to 4 the gap between the map taking x to x and the map taking x to x(1 - 1/5) is largest at the right end. Find that largest gap.
items.s: The gap at x is x/5, which is largest at x = 4, giving 0.8.

items.q: A family of maps has its 3rd member taking x to x/n on the closed stretch from 0 to 2. State 1 if the family settles evenly on that stretch and 0 if it settles only one input at a time.
items.s: The largest gap over the whole stretch is 2/n, which tends to zero, so the settling is even, recorded as 1.

items.q: The sizes of the members of an endless total of maps are never larger than 1/3^n. State the number given by the convergent total of those sizes, to four decimal places.
items.s: The bounding total is geometric with first term 1/3 and ratio 1/3, giving 0.5.

items.q: A set consists of all numbers of the form 3/n where n runs through the counting numbers. Find its supremum.
items.s: The members decrease towards zero as n grows, and the largest is at n = 1, so the least upper bound is 3/1 = 0.75.

items.q: A list has its 3rd member equal to (6 + 6/n) divided by 6. Find the largest value the members of that list can take.
items.s: The members are largest when n is smallest, at n = 1, giving (6 + 6)/6 = 2.

items.q: Find the limit of the list whose 3rd member is (2n + 7) divided by (1n + 13).
items.s: Dividing every term by n leaves 2/1, so the limit is 2.

items.q: Find the limit of the list whose 3rd member is 2 divided by (n + 2).
items.s: The denominator grows without bound while the top stays fixed, so the members approach 0.

items.q: Find the limit of (x^2 - 9)/(x - 3) as x tends to 3.
items.s: Factorising gives x + 3, so as x tends to 3 the value tends to 6.

items.q: A map takes the value 4 for x greater than zero and the value 0 for x less than zero. Find the approach value as x comes towards zero from above.
items.s: For inputs greater than zero the output is constantly 4, so the approach value from above is 4.

items.q: Find the derivative of y = 3x^2 + 6x at x = 1 from the definition as a limit of a ratio of changes.
items.s: The difference quotient simplifies to 6x + 6 with a remainder that vanishes, so at x = 1 the value is 12.

items.q: A stretch of length 2 is split into 4 equal pieces. State the mesh of that split.
items.s: The pieces all have width 2/4, and the mesh is the widest width, which is 0.5.

items.q: A set consists of all numbers of the form 3/(n + 19) where n runs through the counting numbers. Find its infimum.
items.s: The largest denominator gives the smallest member, and as n grows without bound the members approach zero, so the greatest lower bound is 0 = 0.15.

items.q: Find the supremum of the set of all x satisfying 3 < x < 4.
items.s: The members come arbitrarily close to 4 from below without reaching it, so the least upper bound is 3.

items.q: Using the triangle inequality, state the smallest number you can guarantee is at least as large as the size of x + y when the size of x is 6 and the size of y is 6.
items.s: The triangle inequality gives the size of the sum no more than the total of the separate sizes, which is 6 + 6 = 12.

items.q: Find the least counting number n for which n times 0.25 exceeds 2.
items.s: The inequality needs n greater than 2/0.25 = 8, so the least counting number that works is 9.

items.q: A list has its 2nd member equal to 1 - 1/2^n. State 1 if the list never decreases and 0 if it does.
items.s: As n grows the subtracted amount shrinks, so the members grow towards one and never decrease, recorded as 1.

items.q: A list has its 2nd member equal to 5. State 1 if the list satisfies the condition that its members eventually lie arbitrarily close to one another and 0 if it does not.
items.s: A list whose members are all equal certainly satisfies that condition, recorded as 1.

items.q: Which term is described by “the ratio of the change in output to the change in input over a stated stretch”?
o: derivative at a point
difference quotient
one sided derivative
higher order derivative
items.s: difference quotient is the ratio of the change in output to the change in input over a stated stretch.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines jump discontinuity?
o: a gap where the two one sided approach values exist but are not equal
the property that at each separate input the outputs settle on a value, possibly at different rates
the largest number that infinitely many members of a bounded list come arbitrarily close to
the property that the output value equals the approach value at that input
items.s: jump discontinuity: a gap where the two one sided approach values exist but are not equal. The other options describe continuity at a point, limit superior, pointwise convergence.

items.q: squeeze principle may be defined as
o: the statement that a list trapped between two lists sharing one limit must share it too
the total obtained by adding the members of a list one after another
the guarantee that the ratio of two changes over a stretch equals the ratio of two touching slopes at some interior place
the endless total of the reciprocals of the counting numbers
items.s: squeeze principle: the statement that a list trapped between two lists sharing one limit must share it too. The other options describe series, harmonic series, Cauchy mean value form.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines convergent series?
o: the statement that a list trapped between two lists sharing one limit must share it too
the guarantee that a map equal at both ends of a stretch has a place inside where the touching slope is zero
an endless total whose running totals settle down to a finite number
the largest gap between a map and a comparison map over the whole set
items.s: convergent series: an endless total whose running totals settle down to a finite number. The other options describe supremum norm, Rolle theorem, squeeze principle.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines upper bound.
o: the guarantee that the ratio of two changes over a stretch equals the ratio of two touching slopes at some interior place
an endless total whose running totals settle down to a finite number
a number that is at least as large as every member of the set
a finite ordered list of points running from one end of a stretch to the other
items.s: upper bound: a number that is at least as large as every member of the set. The other options describe partition of an interval, Cauchy mean value form, convergent series.

items.q: uniform Cauchy condition may be defined as
o: the requirement that the maps eventually lie close to one another at every input at once
the total obtained by adding the members of a list one after another
a gap where the two one sided approach values exist but are not equal
the requirement that outputs can be kept within any chosen closeness by keeping inputs close enough
items.s: uniform Cauchy condition: the requirement that the maps eventually lie close to one another at every input at once. The other options describe jump discontinuity, series, epsilon delta condition.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines limit superior.
o: the rule that an endless total of smaller positive members converges when one of larger members does
the guarantee that a continuous function taking opposite signs at two places vanishes somewhere between them
an endless total whose members take turns in sign
the largest number that infinitely many members of a bounded list come arbitrarily close to
items.s: limit superior: the largest number that infinitely many members of a bounded list come arbitrarily close to. The other options describe comparison test, alternating series, sign change criterion.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines sequence.
o: the guarantee that a continuous function on a closed bounded stretch attains a largest and a smallest output
a gap where the two sided approach value exists but differs from the value taken there
a gap where the two one sided approach values exist but are not equal
a rule that assigns a real number to each counting number
items.s: sequence: a rule that assigns a real number to each counting number. The other options describe removable discontinuity, extreme value property, jump discontinuity.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines stationary point?
o: a place where the touching slope is zero
the property that at each separate input the outputs settle on a value, possibly at different rates
the total obtained by adding the members of a list one after another
the largest number that infinitely many members of a bounded list come arbitrarily close to
items.s: stationary point: a place where the touching slope is zero. The other options describe limit superior, pointwise convergence, series.

items.q: Which term is described by “a list that possesses no such number”?
o: limit superior
divergent sequence
monotone convergence result
limit of a sequence
items.s: divergent sequence is a list that possesses no such number.

items.q: Which term is described by “a map for which that ratio has a limit at the place in question”?
o: differentiable function
linear approximation
difference quotient
higher order derivative
items.s: differentiable function is a map for which that ratio has a limit at the place in question.

items.q: limit superior may be defined as
o: the property that all the outputs settle at one common rate over the whole set
the largest number that infinitely many members of a bounded list come arbitrarily close to
the rule that compares successive members of an endless total to decide whether the running totals settle
a map for which that ratio has a limit at the place in question
items.s: limit superior: the largest number that infinitely many members of a bounded list come arbitrarily close to. The other options describe differentiable function, uniform convergence, ratio test.

items.q: Which term is described by “a list in which each member is no larger than the one before it”?
o: cluster point of a list
monotone decreasing sequence
Cauchy sequence
subsequence
items.s: monotone decreasing sequence is a list in which each member is no larger than the one before it.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines continuity under uniform limits.
o: the total obtained by adding the members of a list one after another
the guarantee that a continuous function takes every value between any two of its values
the fact that continuous maps whose outputs settle evenly have a continuous limit
the property that all the outputs settle at one common rate over the whole set
items.s: continuity under uniform limits: the fact that continuous maps whose outputs settle evenly have a continuous limit. The other options describe uniform convergence, intermediate value property, series.

items.q: The statement “a finite ordered list of points running from one end of a stretch to the other” describes which of the following?
o: Riemann integrable
monotone integrability
integral as a limit
partition of an interval
items.s: partition of an interval is a finite ordered list of points running from one end of a stretch to the other.

items.q: Which term is described by “the requirement that the maps eventually lie close to one another at every input at once”?
o: uniform Cauchy condition
interchange of limits
power series interval
pointwise convergence
items.s: uniform Cauchy condition is the requirement that the maps eventually lie close to one another at every input at once.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines absolute convergence.
o: the largest number that infinitely many members of a bounded list come arbitrarily close to
the property that the endless total of the sizes of the members is finite
the guarantee that a continuous function on a closed bounded stretch attains a largest and a smallest output
the widest of the pieces into which a stretch has been split
items.s: absolute convergence: the property that the endless total of the sizes of the members is finite. The other options describe extreme value property, mesh of a partition, limit superior.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Rolle theorem.
o: the guarantee that a map equal at both ends of a stretch has a place inside where the touching slope is zero
the total got by using the largest output on each piece of a split stretch
the fact that a map with a limit of the ratio at a place must also be continuous there
the rule that an endless total of maps converges evenly when its sizes are dominated by a convergent total of numbers
items.s: Rolle theorem: the guarantee that a map equal at both ends of a stretch has a place inside where the touching slope is zero. The other options describe differentiability implies continuity, upper sum, Weierstrass test.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines differentiable function?
o: the limit of that ratio taken as the input approaches from a single side only
a member of the set that is at least as large as every other member
the rule that sums, products and quotients of convergent lists converge to the corresponding operations on their limits
a map for which that ratio has a limit at the place in question
items.s: differentiable function: a map for which that ratio has a limit at the place in question. The other options describe one sided derivative, algebra of limits, maximum element.

items.q: divergent sequence may be defined as
o: the guarantee that a continuous function on a closed bounded stretch has outputs lying inside some fixed range
the rule that a positive touching slope throughout a stretch forces the map to rise across it
a list in which each member is no larger than the one before it
a list that possesses no such number
items.s: divergent sequence: a list that possesses no such number. The other options describe monotonicity criterion, monotone decreasing sequence, boundedness on a closed interval.

items.q: Which of the following best describes triangle inequality?
o: the total of the first stated number of members of a list
the part left over when a polynomial approximation is subtracted from the map
the statement that the size of a sum never exceeds the sum of the separate sizes
the rule that a positive touching slope throughout a stretch forces the map to rise across it
items.s: triangle inequality: the statement that the size of a sum never exceeds the sum of the separate sizes. The other options describe monotonicity criterion, remainder term, partial sum.

items.q: Which of the following best describes partition of an interval?
o: a finite ordered list of points running from one end of a stretch to the other
a list whose members eventually lie arbitrarily close to one another
a place where the touching slope is zero
a gap where the two sided approach value exists but differs from the value taken there
items.s: partition of an interval: a finite ordered list of points running from one end of a stretch to the other. The other options describe stationary point, removable discontinuity, Cauchy sequence.

items.q: Which term is described by “the endless total of the reciprocals of the counting numbers”?
o: series
harmonic series
geometric series
absolute convergence
items.s: harmonic series is the endless total of the reciprocals of the counting numbers.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines mean value theorem.
o: the guarantee that every nonempty set bounded above has a least upper bound
the fact that a map with a limit of the ratio at a place must also be continuous there
a place where the touching slope is zero
the guarantee that some interior place has a touching slope equal to the average slope over the whole stretch
items.s: mean value theorem: the guarantee that some interior place has a touching slope equal to the average slope over the whole stretch. The other options describe stationary point, completeness property, differentiability implies continuity.

items.q: uniform continuity may be defined as
o: the property that one closeness of inputs serves for every place in the set
a finite ordered list of points running from one end of a stretch to the other
an endless total whose running totals settle down to a finite number
the statement that the size of a sum never exceeds the sum of the separate sizes
items.s: uniform continuity: the property that one closeness of inputs serves for every place in the set. The other options describe partition of an interval, convergent series, triangle inequality.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Riemann integrable?
o: the property that all the outputs settle at one common rate over the whole set
the guarantee that a continuous function on a closed bounded stretch attains a largest and a smallest output
the property that the upper and lower totals can be brought arbitrarily close together
the use of the touching edge to estimate outputs near a chosen input
items.s: Riemann integrable: the property that the upper and lower totals can be brought arbitrarily close together. The other options describe linear approximation, extreme value property, uniform convergence.

items.q: Which term is described by “the result of applying the differentiating operation repeatedly”?
o: difference quotient
differentiability implies continuity
higher order derivative
derivative at a point
items.s: higher order derivative is the result of applying the differentiating operation repeatedly.

items.q: The statement “the property of being continuous at every member of that set” describes which of the following?
o: epsilon delta condition
algebra of continuous functions
continuous on a set
jump discontinuity
items.s: continuous on a set is the property of being continuous at every member of that set.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines cluster point of a list?
o: the rule that sums, products and quotients of continuous functions are continuous where defined
a number that infinitely many members of the list come arbitrarily close to
the rule that an endless total of smaller positive members converges when one of larger members does
the rule that an endless total of maps converges evenly when its sizes are dominated by a convergent total of numbers
items.s: cluster point of a list: a number that infinitely many members of the list come arbitrarily close to. The other options describe algebra of continuous functions, comparison test, Weierstrass test.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Rolle theorem?
o: the statement that a list trapped between two lists sharing one limit must share it too
the requirement that the maps eventually lie close to one another at every input at once
the guarantee that a map equal at both ends of a stretch has a place inside where the touching slope is zero
a number that is at least as large as every member of the set
items.s: Rolle theorem: the guarantee that a map equal at both ends of a stretch has a place inside where the touching slope is zero. The other options describe squeeze principle, uniform Cauchy condition, upper bound.

items.q: Which term is described by “a list whose members eventually become arbitrarily small in size”?
o: divergent sequence
convergent sequence
limit superior
null sequence
items.s: null sequence is a list whose members eventually become arbitrarily small in size.

items.q: Which term is described by “the total of the first stated number of members of a list”?
o: convergent series
alternating series
partial sum
ratio test
items.s: partial sum is the total of the first stated number of members of a list.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines tail of a sequence?
o: the part that remains after finitely many members have been discarded
a part of the line that meets every open stretch of the line
the guarantee that some interior place has a touching slope equal to the average slope over the whole stretch
the guarantee that a continuous function taking opposite signs at two places vanishes somewhere between them
items.s: tail of a sequence: the part that remains after finitely many members have been discarded. The other options describe dense subset, mean value theorem, sign change criterion.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Cauchy sequence?
o: the total got by using the largest output on each piece of a split stretch
a list whose members eventually lie arbitrarily close to one another
the property of being continuous at every member of that set
an input that the map sends to itself
items.s: Cauchy sequence: a list whose members eventually lie arbitrarily close to one another. The other options describe continuous on a set, fixed point of a map, upper sum.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines local extremum condition?
o: the guarantee that a continuous function on a closed bounded stretch attains a largest and a smallest output
a list in which each member is at least as large as the one before it
the fact that an interior largest or smallest output forces the touching slope to vanish there
the property that one closeness of inputs serves for every place in the set
items.s: local extremum condition: the fact that an interior largest or smallest output forces the touching slope to vanish there. The other options describe uniform continuity, extreme value property, monotone increasing sequence.

items.q: The statement “the guarantee that a multiple of any positive number eventually exceeds any given number” describes which of the following?
o: absolute value
Archimedean property
completeness property
bounded above
items.s: Archimedean property is the guarantee that a multiple of any positive number eventually exceeds any given number.

items.q: Which of the following best describes remainder term?
o: the size of a number with any minus sign removed
a gap where the two sided approach value exists but differs from the value taken there
the part left over when a polynomial approximation is subtracted from the map
the stretch of inputs on which an endless total of powers settles to a finite value
items.s: remainder term: the part left over when a polynomial approximation is subtracted from the map. The other options describe power series interval, absolute value, removable discontinuity.

items.q: The statement “the rule that an endless total of smaller positive members converges when one of larger members does” describes which of the following?
o: partial sum
alternating series
comparison test
series
items.s: comparison test is the rule that an endless total of smaller positive members converges when one of larger members does.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines stationary point.
o: the guarantee that some interior place has a touching slope equal to the average slope over the whole stretch
an endless total in which each member is a fixed multiple of the one before
the property that some number is at least as large as every member of the set
a place where the touching slope is zero
items.s: stationary point: a place where the touching slope is zero. The other options describe bounded above, mean value theorem, geometric series.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines jump discontinuity.
o: the requirement that the maps eventually lie close to one another at every input at once
the result of applying the differentiating operation repeatedly
the rule that an endless total of maps converges evenly when its sizes are dominated by a convergent total of numbers
a gap where the two one sided approach values exist but are not equal
items.s: jump discontinuity: a gap where the two one sided approach values exist but are not equal. The other options describe higher order derivative, Weierstrass test, uniform Cauchy condition.

items.q: Which term is described by “the statement that a list which never decreases and is bounded above must converge”?
o: monotone convergence result
divergent sequence
algebra of limits
squeeze principle
items.s: monotone convergence result is the statement that a list which never decreases and is bounded above must converge.

the largest gap between a map and a comparison map over the whole set
the total obtained by adding the members of a list one after another
the rule that compares successive members of an endless total to decide whether the running totals settle

continuity at a point
epsilon delta condition

ratio test
harmonic series

o: a member of the set that is at least as large as every other member
a list in which each member is no larger than the one before it
the rule that sums, products and quotients of convergent lists converge to the corresponding operations on their limits
a split of a stretch that contains every point of another split

pointwise convergence
uniform convergence
interchange of limits

one sided approach value
continuous on a set
algebra of continuous functions
items.s: one sided approach value is the number that the output tends to as the input comes towards a place from a single side.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines infimum.
o: the guarantee that a map equal at both ends of a stretch has a place inside where the touching slope is zero
an endless total whose running totals settle down to a finite number
the property that one closeness of inputs serves for every place in the set
the greatest of all the lower bounds of a set of numbers
items.s: infimum: the greatest of all the lower bounds of a set of numbers. The other options describe uniform continuity, convergent series, Rolle theorem.

items.q: The statement “the total of the first stated number of members of a list” describes which of the following?
o: absolute convergence
partial sum
harmonic series
ratio test

items.q: Which term is described by “the guarantee that the ratio of two changes over a stretch equals the ratio of two touching slopes at some interior place”?

Cauchy mean value form
remainder term

items.q: Which term is described by “an input that the map sends to itself”?
o: boundedness on a closed interval
Lipschitz condition
root of an equation
fixed point of a map

cluster point of a list
tail of a sequence
subsequence

o: convergent sequence
limit superior
monotone convergence result
limit of a sequence

items.q: Which of the following best describes differentiable function?
o: a map for which that ratio has a limit at the place in question
an endless total whose members take turns in sign
the guarantee that a multiple of any positive number eventually exceeds any given number
the endless total of the reciprocals of the counting numbers
items.s: differentiable function: a map for which that ratio has a limit at the place in question. The other options describe harmonic series, Archimedean property, alternating series.

o: the number that the output tends to as the input comes towards a place from a single side
the step of taking an approach value through an operation on a family of maps
an endless total in which each member is a fixed multiple of the one before
the rule that compares successive members of an endless total to decide whether the running totals settle
items.s: one sided approach value: the number that the output tends to as the input comes towards a place from a single side. The other options describe geometric series, ratio test, interchange of limits.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Archimedean property?
o: a number that infinitely many members of the list come arbitrarily close to
a member of the set that is at least as large as every other member
a finite ordered list of points running from one end of a stretch to the other
the guarantee that a multiple of any positive number eventually exceeds any given number
items.s: Archimedean property: the guarantee that a multiple of any positive number eventually exceeds any given number. The other options describe partition of an interval, maximum element, cluster point of a list.

items.q: integral as a limit may be defined as
o: the number that the output approaches as the input approaches a stated place
a list that possesses no such number
an endless total whose running totals settle down to a finite number
the common number that the upper and lower totals approach as the pieces shrink
items.s: integral as a limit: the common number that the upper and lower totals approach as the pieces shrink. The other options describe divergent sequence, convergent series, limit of a function.

a part of the line that meets every open stretch of the line

the widest of the pieces into which a stretch has been split
the requirement that outputs can be kept within any chosen closeness by keeping inputs close enough
the rule that sums, products and quotients of continuous functions are continuous where defined

the guarantee that some interior place has a touching slope equal to the average slope over the whole stretch
a rule that assigns a real number to each counting number

infimum

Taylor expansion
remainder term

bounded above
dense subset
upper bound

items.q: A list has its 3rd member equal to 1 - 1/4^n. State 1 if the list never decreases and 0 if it does.
items.s: As n grows the subtracted amount shrinks, so the members grow towards one and never decrease, recorded as 1.

items.q: Find the limit of the list whose 3rd member is the square root of (n^2 + 6n) minus n.
items.s: Rationalising gives 6n divided by the square root of (n^2 + 6n) plus n, which tends to 6/2, that is 3.

items.q: Find the limit of the list whose 5th member is (1/2)^n.
items.s: The ratio 1/2 is less than one in size, so powers of it approach 0.

items.q: Find the sum of the endless total 1 + 1/4 + 1/4^2 + ... with common ratio 1/4.
items.s: The sum is the first term divided by one minus the ratio, that is 1/(1 - 1/4) = 1.33.

items.q: A map is given by a polynomial of degree 2 on the whole line. State 1 if it is continuous at every input and 0 if it is not.
items.s: Every polynomial is continuous at every input, so the answer is 1.

items.q: A continuous map takes the value -3 at one place and the value 5 at another. State the number whose existence between those two places is guaranteed by the intermediate value property.
items.s: A continuous map takes every value between -3 and 5, and zero lies between them, so a place where the output is 0 is guaranteed.

items.q: Differentiate y = 2x^3 from first principles and state the value of the derivative at x = 3.
items.s: The difference quotient simplifies to 2nx^2 with a remainder that vanishes, so at x = 3 the value is 54.

items.q: A map takes the value 1 at x = 5 and the value 2 at x = 8. Find the average slope over that stretch.
items.s: The average slope is the change in output divided by the change in input, that is (2 - 1)/3 = 0.3333.

items.q: The 5th member of a family of maps takes x to x/(n + 4). Find the value the outputs settle on at x = 4.
items.s: With x fixed the denominator grows without bound, so the outputs settle on 0.

items.q: A set consists of all numbers of the form 2/n where n runs through the counting numbers. Find its supremum.
items.s: The members decrease towards zero as n grows, and the largest is at n = 1, so the least upper bound is 2/1 = 0.4.

items.q: Find the supremum of the set of all x satisfying 4 < x < 7.
items.s: The members come arbitrarily close to 7 from below without reaching it, so the least upper bound is 4.

items.q: Using the triangle inequality, state the smallest number you can guarantee is at least as large as the size of x + y when the size of x is 4 and the size of y is 2.
items.s: The triangle inequality gives the size of the sum no more than the total of the separate sizes, which is 4 + 2 = 6.

items.q: Find the least counting number n for which n times 0.1 exceeds 3.
items.s: The inequality needs n greater than 3/0.1 = 30, so the least counting number that works is 31.

items.q: A list has its 2nd member equal to (5 + 2/n) divided by 5. Find the largest value the members of that list can take.
items.s: The members are largest when n is smallest, at n = 1, giving (5 + 2)/5 = 1.4.

items.q: Find the limit of the list whose 5th member is (5n + 7) divided by (5n + 13).
items.s: Dividing every term by n leaves 5/5, so the limit is 1.

items.q: Find the limit of the list whose 2nd member is 5 divided by (n + 5).
items.s: The denominator grows without bound while the top stays fixed, so the members approach 0.

items.q: The members of an endless total of positive numbers satisfy the condition that the ratio of successive members tends to 1/2. State the limit of that ratio.
items.s: The ratio tends to 1/2 = 0.5, which is less than one, so the total converges.

items.q: Find the limit of (x^2 - 16)/(x - 4) as x tends to 4.
items.s: Factorising gives x + 4, so as x tends to 4 the value tends to 8.

items.q: Find the limit of sin(4x)/x as x tends to zero.
items.s: Since sin(u)/u tends to one, the quotient tends to 4, that is 4.

items.q: A continuous map on a closed stretch has outputs never below 4 and never above 3. State the smallest number you can guarantee is at least as large as every output of the map there.
items.s: Every output lies between 4 and 3, so 3 is at least as large as every output = 7.

items.q: Find the derivative of y = 3x^2 + 2x at x = 3 from the definition as a limit of a ratio of changes.
items.s: The difference quotient simplifies to 6x + 2 with a remainder that vanishes, so at x = 3 the value is 20.

items.q: Differentiate y equal to the square root of x from first principles and state the value of the derivative at x = 4.
items.s: The derivative is one divided by twice the square root of x, so at x = 4 it is 0.25.

items.q: Write the expansion of e^(2x) about zero as far as the term in x^2. State the coefficient of that term.
items.s: The coefficient is 2^2 divided by 2 factorial, which is 0.5.

items.q: For the map taking x to x^2 on the stretch from 0 to 2, split the stretch into 2 equal pieces and use the largest output on each piece. Find the resulting upper total.
items.s: The largest output on each piece is at its right end, and summing gives 5.

items.q: For the map taking x to x^2 on the stretch from 0 to 4, split the stretch into 4 equal pieces and use the smallest output on each piece. Find the resulting lower total.
items.s: The smallest output on each piece is at its left end, and summing gives 14.

items.q: For the map taking x to x^2 on the stretch from 0 to 3 split into 4 equal pieces, find the gap between the upper total and the lower total.
items.s: The two totals differ only in the last piece, and the gap is 3^2 times the width 0.75, giving 6.75.

items.q: A stretch of length 1 is split into 5 equal pieces. State the mesh of that split.
items.s: The pieces all have width 1/5, and the mesh is the widest width, which is 0.2.

items.q: A map never decreases on the closed stretch from 0 to 3. State 1 if it can certainly be integrated there and 0 if it cannot.
items.s: A map that never decreases on a closed stretch can always be integrated there, so the answer is 1.

items.q: On the stretch from 0 to 2 the gap between the map taking x to x and the map taking x to x(1 - 1/3) is largest at the right end. Find that largest gap.
items.s: The gap at x is x/3, which is largest at x = 2, giving 0.6667.

items.q: A family of maps has its 3rd member taking x to x/n on the closed stretch from 0 to 3. State 1 if the family settles evenly on that stretch and 0 if it settles only one input at a time.
items.s: The largest gap over the whole stretch is 3/n, which tends to zero, so the settling is even, recorded as 1.

items.q: A list has its 2nd member equal to 1 - 1/3^n. State 1 if the list never decreases and 0 if it does.
items.s: As n grows the subtracted amount shrinks, so the members grow towards one and never decrease, recorded as 1.

items.q: Find the limit of the list whose 2nd member is the square root of (n^2 + 4n) minus n.
items.s: Rationalising gives 4n divided by the square root of (n^2 + 4n) plus n, which tends to 4/2, that is 2.

items.q: Find the limit of the list whose 3rd member is (3/4)^n.
items.s: The ratio 3/4 is less than one in size, so powers of it approach 0.

items.q: Find the sum of the endless total 1 + 1/6 + 1/6^2 + ... with common ratio 1/6.
items.s: The sum is the first term divided by one minus the ratio, that is 1/(1 - 1/6) = 1.2.

items.q: Find the sum of the first 6 members of the endless total 1 + 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + ...
items.s: The sum of the first 6 members is 2 minus the remainder after 6 terms, which is 6 to four decimal places.

items.q: A continuous map takes the value -4 at one place and the value 3 at another. State the number whose existence between those two places is guaranteed by the intermediate value property.
items.s: A continuous map takes every value between -4 and 3, and zero lies between them, so a place where the output is 0 is guaranteed.

items.q: Differentiate y = 4x^3 from first principles and state the value of the derivative at x = 2.
items.s: The difference quotient simplifies to 4nx^2 with a remainder that vanishes, so at x = 2 the value is 48.

items.q: A map takes the value -3 at x = 1 and the value 0 at x = 4. Find the average slope over that stretch.
items.s: The average slope is the change in output divided by the change in input, that is (0 - -3)/3 = 1.

items.q: A map equals zero at x = 2 and at x = 3. Find the place inside the stretch where the guarantee of Rolle applies forces the touching slope to be zero, for the quadratic passing through both.
items.s: The place is halfway between 2 and 3, that is 2.5.

items.q: The 2nd member of a family of maps takes x to x/(n + 4). Find the value the outputs settle on at x = 2.
items.s: With x fixed the denominator grows without bound, so the outputs settle on 0.

items.q: Find the supremum of the set of all x satisfying 1 < x < 5.
items.s: The members come arbitrarily close to 5 from below without reaching it, so the least upper bound is 1.

items.q: Using the triangle inequality, state the smallest number you can guarantee is at least as large as the size of x + y when the size of x is 6 and the size of y is 8.
items.s: The triangle inequality gives the size of the sum no more than the total of the separate sizes, which is 6 + 8 = 14.

items.q: A list has its 3rd member equal to (4 + 6/n) divided by 4. Find the largest value the members of that list can take.
items.s: The members are largest when n is smallest, at n = 1, giving (4 + 6)/4 = 2.5.

items.q: A list converges to 3. Find the limit of the list obtained by keeping only the members in even positions.
items.s: Any part built by keeping members in their original order converges to the same value, so the limit stays 3.

items.q: A list has its 2nd member equal to 2. State 1 if the list satisfies the condition that its members eventually lie arbitrarily close to one another and 0 if it does not.
items.s: A list whose members are all equal certainly satisfies that condition, recorded as 1.

items.q: Find the limit of the list whose 5th member is (5n + 7) divided by (2n + 9).
items.s: Dividing every term by n leaves 5/2, so the limit is 2.5.

items.q: Find the limit of the list whose 5th member is 3 divided by n multiplied by the sine of n.
items.s: The sine never exceeds one in size, so the members are trapped between plus and minus 3/n, both of which approach 0; the limit is therefore 0.

items.q: Find the limit of (x^2 - 25)/(x - 5) as x tends to 5.
items.s: Factorising gives x + 5, so as x tends to 5 the value tends to 10.

items.q: Find the limit of sin(6x)/x as x tends to zero.
items.s: Since sin(u)/u tends to one, the quotient tends to 6, that is 6.

items.q: A continuous map on the closed stretch from 0 to 2 has its largest output equal to 16. State the largest output of the map on that stretch.
items.s: The extreme value property guarantees that the largest output is actually attained, and it is given as 16.

items.q: A continuous map on a closed stretch has outputs never below 6 and never above 6. State the smallest number you can guarantee is at least as large as every output of the map there.
items.s: Every output lies between 6 and 6, so 6 is at least as large as every output = 12.

items.q: Find the derivative of y = 3x^2 + 2x at x = 2 from the definition as a limit of a ratio of changes.
items.s: The difference quotient simplifies to 6x + 2 with a remainder that vanishes, so at x = 2 the value is 14.

items.q: A differentiable map has the same value at x = 0 and at x = 4. State the least number of places inside the stretch where the touching slope is zero that the guarantee forces.
items.s: The guarantee forces at least one such place inside the stretch, recorded as 1.

items.q: Write the expansion of e^(4x) about zero as far as the term in x^3. State the coefficient of that term.
items.s: The coefficient is 4^3 divided by 3 factorial, which is 0.1667.

items.q: For the map taking x to x^2 on the stretch from 0 to 4, split the stretch into 4 equal pieces and use the largest output on each piece. Find the resulting upper total.
items.s: The largest output on each piece is at its right end, and summing gives 30.

items.q: For the map taking x to x^2 on the stretch from 0 to 4, split the stretch into 2 equal pieces and use the smallest output on each piece. Find the resulting lower total.
items.s: The smallest output on each piece is at its left end, and summing gives 8.

items.q: For the map taking x to x^2 on the stretch from 0 to 2 split into 2 equal pieces, find the gap between the upper total and the lower total.
items.s: The two totals differ only in the last piece, and the gap is 2^2 times the width 1, giving 4.

items.q: A map never decreases on the closed stretch from 0 to 4. State 1 if it can certainly be integrated there and 0 if it cannot.
items.s: A map that never decreases on a closed stretch can always be integrated there, so the answer is 1.

items.q: On the stretch from 0 to 4 the gap between the map taking x to x and the map taking x to x(1 - 1/3) is largest at the right end. Find that largest gap.
items.s: The gap at x is x/3, which is largest at x = 4, giving 1.33.

items.q: A family of maps has its 3rd member taking x to x/n on the closed stretch from 0 to 4. State 1 if the family settles evenly on that stretch and 0 if it settles only one input at a time.
items.s: The largest gap over the whole stretch is 4/n, which tends to zero, so the settling is even, recorded as 1.

the rule that sums, products and quotients of convergent lists converge to the corresponding operations on their limits
a list whose members eventually become arbitrarily small in size

continuity at a point

bounded above
triangle inequality

limit of a function
continuous on a set

one sided derivative
derivative at a point

supremum norm

the property that all the outputs settle at one common rate over the whole set
the step of taking an approach value through an operation on a family of maps

series
ratio test

the rule that sums, products and quotients of convergent lists converge to the corresponding operations on their limits
a list that possesses no such number
