the guarantee that some interior place has a touching slope equal to the average slope over the whole stretch
the part left over when a polynomial approximation is subtracted from the map
the rule that a positive touching slope throughout a stretch forces the map to rise across it
items.s: mean value theorem: the guarantee that some interior place has a touching slope equal to the average slope over the whole stretch. The other options describe stationary point, remainder term, monotonicity criterion.

items.q: The best definition of completeness property among these is
o: the size of a number with any minus sign removed
the guarantee that every nonempty set bounded above has a least upper bound
the least of all the upper bounds of a set of numbers
the property that some number is at least as large as every member of the set
items.s: completeness property: the guarantee that every nonempty set bounded above has a least upper bound. The other options describe supremum, bounded above, absolute value.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what partial sum means.
o: an endless total whose members take turns in sign
the rule that an endless total of smaller positive members converges when one of larger members does
the total of the first stated number of members of a list
an endless total in which each member is a fixed multiple of the one before
items.s: partial sum: the total of the first stated number of members of a list. The other options describe geometric series, alternating series, comparison test.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the least of all the upper bounds of a set of numbers”
o: maximum element
supremum
dense subset
Archimedean property
items.s: supremum is the least of all the upper bounds of a set of numbers.

items.q: Which term is described by “the guarantee that a multiple of any positive number eventually exceeds any given number”?
o: dense subset
Archimedean property
bounded above
supremum
items.s: Archimedean property is the guarantee that a multiple of any positive number eventually exceeds any given number.

items.q: All of the following belong to The Riemann integral EXCEPT
o: monotonicity criterion
partition of an interval
lower sum
upper sum
items.s: Every other option belongs to The Riemann integral. “monotonicity criterion” belongs to The mean value theorems, not The Riemann integral.

items.q: In this course, supremum refers to
o: the guarantee that a multiple of any positive number eventually exceeds any given number
the greatest of all the lower bounds of a set of numbers
a part of the line that meets every open stretch of the line
the least of all the upper bounds of a set of numbers
items.s: supremum: the least of all the upper bounds of a set of numbers. The other options describe infimum, Archimedean property, dense subset.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what local extremum condition means.
o: the guarantee that a map equal at both ends of a stretch has a place inside where the touching slope is zero
the writing of a map as a polynomial about a chosen place plus a remainder
the fact that an interior largest or smallest output forces the touching slope to vanish there
the rule that a positive touching slope throughout a stretch forces the map to rise across it
items.s: local extremum condition: the fact that an interior largest or smallest output forces the touching slope to vanish there. The other options describe Rolle theorem, monotonicity criterion, Taylor expansion.

items.q: derivative at a point is best described as
o: the limit of the ratio of the change in output to the change in input as the latter shrinks
the limit of that ratio taken as the input approaches from a single side only
the fact that a map with a limit of the ratio at a place must also be continuous there
the use of the touching edge to estimate outputs near a chosen input
items.s: derivative at a point: the limit of the ratio of the change in output to the change in input as the latter shrinks. The other options describe one sided derivative, differentiability implies continuity, linear approximation.

items.q: The best definition of monotone convergence result among these is
o: a list that possesses a number its members eventually stay arbitrarily close to
the statement that a list which never decreases and is bounded above must converge
the largest number that infinitely many members of a bounded list come arbitrarily close to
a list whose members eventually become arbitrarily small in size
items.s: monotone convergence result: the statement that a list which never decreases and is bounded above must converge. The other options describe limit superior, null sequence, convergent sequence.

items.q: Which term is described by “the total obtained by adding the members of a list one after another”?
o: comparison test
series
alternating series
convergent series
items.s: series is the total obtained by adding the members of a list one after another.

items.q: ratio test is best described as
o: the property that the endless total of the sizes of the members is finite
the rule that compares successive members of an endless total to decide whether the running totals settle
the total of the first stated number of members of a list
an endless total whose members take turns in sign
items.s: ratio test: the rule that compares successive members of an endless total to decide whether the running totals settle. The other options describe absolute convergence, alternating series, partial sum.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the total got by using the largest output on each piece of a split stretch”
o: Riemann integrable
partition of an interval
upper sum
monotone integrability
items.s: upper sum is the total got by using the largest output on each piece of a split stretch.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a gap where the two sided approach value exists but differs from the value taken there”
o: limit of a function
jump discontinuity
removable discontinuity
algebra of continuous functions
items.s: removable discontinuity is a gap where the two sided approach value exists but differs from the value taken there.

items.q: The statement “the guarantee that a continuous function on a closed bounded stretch has outputs lying inside some fixed range” describes which of the following?
o: fixed point of a map
sign change criterion
boundedness on a closed interval
Lipschitz condition
items.s: boundedness on a closed interval is the guarantee that a continuous function on a closed bounded stretch has outputs lying inside some fixed range.

items.q: The best definition of monotone decreasing sequence among these is
o: a rule that assigns a real number to each counting number
a list in which each member is no larger than the one before it
a list whose members all lie inside some fixed stretch of the line
the part that remains after finitely many members have been discarded
items.s: monotone decreasing sequence: a list in which each member is no larger than the one before it. The other options describe bounded sequence, tail of a sequence, sequence.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what continuity under uniform limits means.
o: the fact that continuous maps whose outputs settle evenly have a continuous limit
the property that all the outputs settle at one common rate over the whole set
the property that at each separate input the outputs settle on a value, possibly at different rates
the largest gap between a map and a comparison map over the whole set
items.s: continuity under uniform limits: the fact that continuous maps whose outputs settle evenly have a continuous limit. The other options describe supremum norm, pointwise convergence, uniform convergence.

items.q: Which term is described by “the rule that compares successive members of an endless total to decide whether the running totals settle”?
o: ratio test
absolute convergence
series
convergent series
items.s: ratio test is the rule that compares successive members of an endless total to decide whether the running totals settle.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what bounded above means.
o: the size of a number with any minus sign removed
the statement that the size of a sum never exceeds the sum of the separate sizes
a member of the set that is at least as large as every other member
the property that some number is at least as large as every member of the set
items.s: bounded above: the property that some number is at least as large as every member of the set. The other options describe absolute value, triangle inequality, maximum element.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Weierstrass test means.
o: the requirement that the maps eventually lie close to one another at every input at once
the rule that an endless total of maps converges evenly when its sizes are dominated by a convergent total of numbers
the fact that continuous maps whose outputs settle evenly have a continuous limit
the property that all the outputs settle at one common rate over the whole set
items.s: Weierstrass test: the rule that an endless total of maps converges evenly when its sizes are dominated by a convergent total of numbers. The other options describe continuity under uniform limits, uniform Cauchy condition, uniform convergence.

items.q: limit superior is best described as
o: the statement that a list trapped between two lists sharing one limit must share it too
a list that possesses no such number
the largest number that infinitely many members of a bounded list come arbitrarily close to
the rule that sums, products and quotients of convergent lists converge to the corresponding operations on their limits
items.s: limit superior: the largest number that infinitely many members of a bounded list come arbitrarily close to. The other options describe squeeze principle, divergent sequence, algebra of limits.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what absolute convergence means.
o: the property that the endless total of the sizes of the members is finite
the total of the first stated number of members of a list
the rule that an endless total of smaller positive members converges when one of larger members does
the endless total of the reciprocals of the counting numbers
items.s: absolute convergence: the property that the endless total of the sizes of the members is finite. The other options describe comparison test, harmonic series, partial sum.

items.q: tail of a sequence is best described as
o: a rule that assigns a real number to each counting number
a number that infinitely many members of the list come arbitrarily close to
a list obtained by keeping infinitely many members of a given list in their original order
the part that remains after finitely many members have been discarded
items.s: tail of a sequence: the part that remains after finitely many members have been discarded. The other options describe subsequence, cluster point of a list, sequence.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the total obtained by adding the members of a list one after another”
o: series
geometric series
alternating series
harmonic series
items.s: series is the total obtained by adding the members of a list one after another.

items.q: The statement “the requirement that the maps eventually lie close to one another at every input at once” describes which of the following?
o: power series interval
continuity under uniform limits
interchange of limits
uniform Cauchy condition
items.s: uniform Cauchy condition is the requirement that the maps eventually lie close to one another at every input at once.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what sequence means.
o: a number that infinitely many members of the list come arbitrarily close to
the part that remains after finitely many members have been discarded
a list whose members eventually lie arbitrarily close to one another
a rule that assigns a real number to each counting number
items.s: sequence: a rule that assigns a real number to each counting number. The other options describe tail of a sequence, cluster point of a list, Cauchy sequence.

items.q: Taylor expansion is best described as
o: the guarantee that some interior place has a touching slope equal to the average slope over the whole stretch
a place where the touching slope is zero
the part left over when a polynomial approximation is subtracted from the map
the writing of a map as a polynomial about a chosen place plus a remainder
items.s: Taylor expansion: the writing of a map as a polynomial about a chosen place plus a remainder. The other options describe mean value theorem, remainder term, stationary point.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what difference quotient means.
o: the ratio of the change in output to the change in input over a stated stretch
the number giving the steepness of the touching edge at a place
the result of applying the differentiating operation repeatedly
the limit of the ratio of the change in output to the change in input as the latter shrinks
items.s: difference quotient: the ratio of the change in output to the change in input over a stated stretch. The other options describe derivative at a point, higher order derivative, tangent slope.

items.q: absolute convergence is best described as
o: an endless total in which each member is a fixed multiple of the one before
the property that the endless total of the sizes of the members is finite
the total obtained by adding the members of a list one after another
an endless total whose members take turns in sign
items.s: absolute convergence: the property that the endless total of the sizes of the members is finite. The other options describe alternating series, series, geometric series.

items.q: In this course, local extremum condition refers to
o: the part left over when a polynomial approximation is subtracted from the map
a place where the touching slope is zero
the fact that an interior largest or smallest output forces the touching slope to vanish there
the guarantee that the ratio of two changes over a stretch equals the ratio of two touching slopes at some interior place
items.s: local extremum condition: the fact that an interior largest or smallest output forces the touching slope to vanish there. The other options describe stationary point, remainder term, Cauchy mean value form.

items.q: uniform convergence is best described as
o: the rule that an endless total of maps converges evenly when its sizes are dominated by a convergent total of numbers
the property that all the outputs settle at one common rate over the whole set
the fact that continuous maps whose outputs settle evenly have a continuous limit
the largest gap between a map and a comparison map over the whole set
items.s: uniform convergence: the property that all the outputs settle at one common rate over the whole set. The other options describe supremum norm, Weierstrass test, continuity under uniform limits.

items.q: In this course, partition of an interval refers to
o: the property that the upper and lower totals can be brought arbitrarily close together
a split of a stretch that contains every point of another split
the widest of the pieces into which a stretch has been split
a finite ordered list of points running from one end of a stretch to the other
items.s: partition of an interval: a finite ordered list of points running from one end of a stretch to the other. The other options describe refinement, Riemann integrable, mesh of a partition.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what monotone decreasing sequence means.
o: a list whose members eventually lie arbitrarily close to one another
a list in which each member is no larger than the one before it
the part that remains after finitely many members have been discarded
a list in which each member is at least as large as the one before it
items.s: monotone decreasing sequence: a list in which each member is no larger than the one before it. The other options describe monotone increasing sequence, Cauchy sequence, tail of a sequence.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what remainder term means.
o: the writing of a map as a polynomial about a chosen place plus a remainder
the guarantee that some interior place has a touching slope equal to the average slope over the whole stretch
a place where the touching slope is zero
the part left over when a polynomial approximation is subtracted from the map
items.s: remainder term: the part left over when a polynomial approximation is subtracted from the map. The other options describe stationary point, mean value theorem, Taylor expansion.

items.q: The best definition of extreme value property among these is
o: the guarantee that a continuous function on a closed bounded stretch attains a largest and a smallest output
the guarantee that a continuous function on a closed bounded stretch has outputs lying inside some fixed range
the requirement that the change in output never exceeds a fixed multiple of the change in input
an input at which the output is zero
items.s: extreme value property: the guarantee that a continuous function on a closed bounded stretch attains a largest and a smallest output. The other options describe boundedness on a closed interval, root of an equation, Lipschitz condition.

items.q: The statement “a number that is at least as large as every member of the set” describes which of the following?
o: completeness property
supremum
absolute value
upper bound
items.s: upper bound is a number that is at least as large as every member of the set.

items.q: In this course, root of an equation refers to
o: an input at which the output is zero
the guarantee that a continuous function takes every value between any two of its values
an input that the map sends to itself
the requirement that the change in output never exceeds a fixed multiple of the change in input
items.s: root of an equation: an input at which the output is zero. The other options describe fixed point of a map, intermediate value property, Lipschitz condition.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the limit of the ratio of the change in output to the change in input as the latter shrinks”
o: derivative at a point
differentiable function
differentiability implies continuity
difference quotient
items.s: derivative at a point is the limit of the ratio of the change in output to the change in input as the latter shrinks.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what higher order derivative means.
o: a map for which that ratio has a limit at the place in question
the fact that a map with a limit of the ratio at a place must also be continuous there
the result of applying the differentiating operation repeatedly
the number giving the steepness of the touching edge at a place
items.s: higher order derivative: the result of applying the differentiating operation repeatedly. The other options describe tangent slope, differentiability implies continuity, differentiable function.

items.q: The statement “the fact that an interior largest or smallest output forces the touching slope to vanish there” describes which of the following?
o: local extremum condition
remainder term
Taylor expansion
mean value theorem
items.s: local extremum condition is the fact that an interior largest or smallest output forces the touching slope to vanish there.

items.q: In this course, null sequence refers to
o: a list that possesses no such number
the rule that sums, products and quotients of convergent lists converge to the corresponding operations on their limits
a list whose members eventually become arbitrarily small in size
the largest number that infinitely many members of a bounded list come arbitrarily close to
items.s: null sequence: a list whose members eventually become arbitrarily small in size. The other options describe divergent sequence, algebra of limits, limit superior.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what mean value theorem means.
o: the guarantee that some interior place has a touching slope equal to the average slope over the whole stretch
the part left over when a polynomial approximation is subtracted from the map
the rule that a positive touching slope throughout a stretch forces the map to rise across it
the writing of a map as a polynomial about a chosen place plus a remainder
items.s: mean value theorem: the guarantee that some interior place has a touching slope equal to the average slope over the whole stretch. The other options describe Taylor expansion, remainder term, monotonicity criterion.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what monotone integrability means.
o: the fact that a map which never decreases on a closed stretch can always be integrated there
the property that the upper and lower totals can be brought arbitrarily close together
the total got by using the largest output on each piece of a split stretch
the total got by using the smallest output on each piece of a split stretch
items.s: monotone integrability: the fact that a map which never decreases on a closed stretch can always be integrated there. The other options describe lower sum, upper sum, Riemann integrable.

items.q: Which term is described by “an endless total whose members take turns in sign”?
o: comparison test
absolute convergence
alternating series
partial sum
items.s: alternating series is an endless total whose members take turns in sign.

items.q: The best definition of local extremum condition among these is
o: the fact that an interior largest or smallest output forces the touching slope to vanish there
the writing of a map as a polynomial about a chosen place plus a remainder
the rule that a positive touching slope throughout a stretch forces the map to rise across it
a place where the touching slope is zero
items.s: local extremum condition: the fact that an interior largest or smallest output forces the touching slope to vanish there. The other options describe monotonicity criterion, Taylor expansion, stationary point.

items.q: The best definition of continuity at a point among these is
o: the property of being continuous at every member of that set
a gap where the two sided approach value exists but differs from the value taken there
the number that the output tends to as the input comes towards a place from a single side
the property that the output value equals the approach value at that input
items.s: continuity at a point: the property that the output value equals the approach value at that input. The other options describe removable discontinuity, continuous on a set, one sided approach value.

items.q: The statement “the guarantee that a continuous function taking opposite signs at two places vanishes somewhere between them” describes which of the following?
o: sign change criterion
uniform continuity
boundedness on a closed interval
root of an equation
items.s: sign change criterion is the guarantee that a continuous function taking opposite signs at two places vanishes somewhere between them.

items.q: Using the triangle inequality, state the smallest number you can guarantee is at least as large as the size of x + y when the size of x is 3 and the size of y is 3.
items.s: The triangle inequality gives the size of the sum no more than the total of the separate sizes, which is 3 + 3 = 6.

items.q: A list converges to 2. Find the limit of the list obtained by keeping only the members in even positions.
items.s: Any part built by keeping members in their original order converges to the same value, so the limit stays 2.

items.q: Find the limit of the list whose 3rd member is 2 divided by n multiplied by the sine of n.
items.s: The sine never exceeds one in size, so the members are trapped between plus and minus 2/n, both of which approach 0; the limit is therefore 0.

items.q: The members of an endless total of positive numbers satisfy the condition that the ratio of successive members tends to 1/4. State the limit of that ratio.
items.s: The ratio tends to 1/4 = 0.25, which is less than one, so the total converges.

items.q: A continuous map on the closed stretch from 0 to 2 has its largest output equal to 4. State the largest output of the map on that stretch.
items.s: The extreme value property guarantees that the largest output is actually attained, and it is given as 4.

items.q: A continuous map on a closed stretch has outputs never below 5 and never above 6. State the smallest number you can guarantee is at least as large as every output of the map there.
items.s: Every output lies between 5 and 6, so 6 is at least as large as every output = 11.

items.q: Differentiate y equal to the square root of x from first principles and state the value of the derivative at x = 9.
items.s: The derivative is one divided by twice the square root of x, so at x = 9 it is 0.1667.

items.q: Write the expansion of e^(2x) about zero as far as the term in x^3. State the coefficient of that term.
items.s: The coefficient is 2^3 divided by 3 factorial, which is 0.1667.

items.q: On the stretch from 0 to 2 the gap between the map taking x to x and the map taking x to x(1 - 1/10) is largest at the right end. Find that largest gap.
items.s: The gap at x is x/10, which is largest at x = 2, giving 0.2.

items.q: A set consists of all numbers of the form 4/n where n runs through the counting numbers. Find its supremum.
items.s: The members decrease towards zero as n grows, and the largest is at n = 1, so the least upper bound is 4/1 = 1.33.

items.q: A set consists of all numbers of the form 5/(n + 19) where n runs through the counting numbers. Find its infimum.
items.s: The largest denominator gives the smallest member, and as n grows without bound the members approach zero, so the greatest lower bound is 0 = 0.25.

items.q: Find the least counting number n for which n times 0.25 exceeds 3.
items.s: The inequality needs n greater than 3/0.25 = 12, so the least counting number that works is 13.

items.q: A list has its 5th member equal to (5 + 3/n) divided by 5. Find the largest value the members of that list can take.
items.s: The members are largest when n is smallest, at n = 1, giving (5 + 3)/5 = 1.6.

items.q: A list has its 4th member equal to 2. State 1 if the list satisfies the condition that its members eventually lie arbitrarily close to one another and 0 if it does not.
items.s: A list whose members are all equal certainly satisfies that condition, recorded as 1.

items.q: Find the limit of the list whose 2nd member is (5n + 7) divided by (2n + 13).
items.s: Dividing every term by n leaves 5/2, so the limit is 2.5.

items.q: Find the limit of the list whose 5th member is 3 divided by (n + 3).
items.s: The denominator grows without bound while the top stays fixed, so the members approach 0.

items.q: Find the limit of the list whose 3rd member is the square root of (n^2 + 2n) minus n.
items.s: Rationalising gives 2n divided by the square root of (n^2 + 2n) plus n, which tends to 2/2, that is 1.

items.q: Find the sum of the first 20 members of the endless total 1 + 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + ...
items.s: The sum of the first 20 members is 2 minus the remainder after 20 terms, which is 20 to four decimal places.

items.q: Find the limit of (x^2 - 36)/(x - 6) as x tends to 6.
items.s: Factorising gives x + 6, so as x tends to 6 the value tends to 12.

items.q: A continuous map takes the value -4 at one place and the value 2 at another. State the number whose existence between those two places is guaranteed by the intermediate value property.
items.s: A continuous map takes every value between -4 and 2, and zero lies between them, so a place where the output is 0 is guaranteed.

items.q: Find the derivative of y = 1x^2 + 4x at x = 3 from the definition as a limit of a ratio of changes.
items.s: The difference quotient simplifies to 2x + 4 with a remainder that vanishes, so at x = 3 the value is 10.

items.q: Differentiate y = 2x^2 from first principles and state the value of the derivative at x = 3.
items.s: The difference quotient simplifies to 2nx^1 with a remainder that vanishes, so at x = 3 the value is 12.

items.q: A map takes the value -1 at x = 4 and the value -4 at x = 6. Find the average slope over that stretch.
items.s: The average slope is the change in output divided by the change in input, that is (-4 - -1)/2 = -1.5.

items.q: A map equals zero at x = 1 and at x = 3. Find the place inside the stretch where the guarantee of Rolle applies forces the touching slope to be zero, for the quadratic passing through both.
items.s: The place is halfway between 1 and 3, that is 2.

items.q: The expansion of a map about zero is stopped after the term in x^3. State the power of x with which the remainder term begins, for a map whose derivatives of all orders exist.
items.s: Stopping after the term in x^3 leaves a remainder beginning with the power x^4.

items.q: For the map taking x to x^2 on the stretch from 0 to 2 split into 4 equal pieces, find the gap between the upper total and the lower total.
items.s: The two totals differ only in the last piece, and the gap is 2^2 times the width 0.5, giving 2.

items.q: A stretch of length 3 is split into 8 equal pieces. State the mesh of that split.
items.s: The pieces all have width 3/8, and the mesh is the widest width, which is 0.375.

items.q: Find the supremum of the set of all x satisfying 6 < x < 8.
items.s: The members come arbitrarily close to 8 from below without reaching it, so the least upper bound is 6.

items.q: Using the triangle inequality, state the smallest number you can guarantee is at least as large as the size of x + y when the size of x is 6 and the size of y is 4.
items.s: The triangle inequality gives the size of the sum no more than the total of the separate sizes, which is 6 + 4 = 10.

items.q: Find the limit of the list whose 3rd member is 4 divided by n multiplied by the sine of n.
items.s: The sine never exceeds one in size, so the members are trapped between plus and minus 4/n, both of which approach 0; the limit is therefore 0.

items.q: The members of an endless total of positive numbers satisfy the condition that the ratio of successive members tends to 1/3. State the limit of that ratio.
items.s: The ratio tends to 1/3 = 0.3333, which is less than one, so the total converges.

items.q: Find the limit of sin(3x)/x as x tends to zero.
items.s: Since sin(u)/u tends to one, the quotient tends to 3, that is 3.

items.q: A continuous map on the closed stretch from 0 to 3 has its largest output equal to 16. State the largest output of the map on that stretch.
items.s: The extreme value property guarantees that the largest output is actually attained, and it is given as 16.

items.q: A continuous map on a closed stretch has outputs never below 2 and never above 5. State the smallest number you can guarantee is at least as large as every output of the map there.
items.s: Every output lies between 2 and 5, so 5 is at least as large as every output = 7.

items.q: Differentiate y = 2/x from first principles and state the value of the derivative at x = 2.
items.s: The difference quotient tends to minus 2 divided by x squared, so at x = 2 the value is -0.5.

items.q: Differentiate y equal to the square root of x from first principles and state the value of the derivative at x = 16.
items.s: The derivative is one divided by twice the square root of x, so at x = 16 it is 0.125.

items.q: A differentiable map has the same value at x = 0 and at x = 3. State the least number of places inside the stretch where the touching slope is zero that the guarantee forces.
items.s: The guarantee forces at least one such place inside the stretch, recorded as 1.

items.q: For the map taking x to x^2 on the stretch from 0 to 4, split the stretch into 2 equal pieces and use the largest output on each piece. Find the resulting upper total.
items.s: The largest output on each piece is at its right end, and summing gives 40.

items.q: A set consists of all numbers of the form 5/(n + 29) where n runs through the counting numbers. Find its infimum.
items.s: The largest denominator gives the smallest member, and as n grows without bound the members approach zero, so the greatest lower bound is 0 = 0.1667.

items.q: Find the least counting number n for which n times 0.2 exceeds 1.
items.s: The inequality needs n greater than 1/0.2 = 5, so the least counting number that works is 6.

items.q: A list has its 3rd member equal to (4 + 3/n) divided by 4. Find the largest value the members of that list can take.
items.s: The members are largest when n is smallest, at n = 1, giving (4 + 3)/4 = 1.75.

items.q: Find the limit of the list whose 5th member is (5n + 11) divided by (2n + 13).
items.s: Dividing every term by n leaves 5/2, so the limit is 2.5.

items.q: Find the limit of the list whose 3rd member is 4 divided by (n + 4).
items.s: The denominator grows without bound while the top stays fixed, so the members approach 0.

items.q: Find the limit of the list whose 5th member is (2/3)^n.
items.s: The ratio 2/3 is less than one in size, so powers of it approach 0.

items.q: A map is given by a polynomial of degree 4 on the whole line. State 1 if it is continuous at every input and 0 if it is not.
items.s: Every polynomial is continuous at every input, so the answer is 1.

items.q: A continuous map takes the value -2 at one place and the value 3 at another. State the number whose existence between those two places is guaranteed by the intermediate value property.
items.s: A continuous map takes every value between -2 and 3, and zero lies between them, so a place where the output is 0 is guaranteed.

items.q: Find the derivative of y = 1x^2 + 6x at x = 1 from the definition as a limit of a ratio of changes.
items.s: The difference quotient simplifies to 2x + 6 with a remainder that vanishes, so at x = 1 the value is 8.

items.q: Differentiate y = 3x^2 from first principles and state the value of the derivative at x = 1.
items.s: The difference quotient simplifies to 3nx^1 with a remainder that vanishes, so at x = 1 the value is 6.

items.q: A map takes the value -2 at x = 5 and the value -3 at x = 10. Find the average slope over that stretch.
items.s: The average slope is the change in output divided by the change in input, that is (-3 - -2)/5 = -0.2.

items.q: A family of maps has its 2nd member taking x to x/n on the closed stretch from 0 to 3. State 1 if the family settles evenly on that stretch and 0 if it settles only one input at a time.
items.s: The largest gap over the whole stretch is 3/n, which tends to zero, so the settling is even, recorded as 1.

items.q: The sizes of the members of an endless total of maps are never larger than 1/2^n. State the number given by the convergent total of those sizes, to four decimal places.
items.s: The bounding total is geometric with first term 1/2 and ratio 1/2, giving 1.

items.q: Find the supremum of the set of all x satisfying 6 < x < 10.
items.s: The members come arbitrarily close to 10 from below without reaching it, so the least upper bound is 6.

items.q: Using the triangle inequality, state the smallest number you can guarantee is at least as large as the size of x + y when the size of x is 7 and the size of y is 5.
items.s: The triangle inequality gives the size of the sum no more than the total of the separate sizes, which is 7 + 5 = 12.

items.q: A list has its 5th member equal to (5 + 2/n) divided by 5. Find the largest value the members of that list can take.
items.s: The members are largest when n is smallest, at n = 1, giving (5 + 2)/5 = 1.4.

items.q: Find the limit of the list whose 2nd member is (4n + 7) divided by (4n + 13).
items.s: Dividing every term by n leaves 4/4, so the limit is 1.

items.q: Find the limit of the list whose 5th member is 4 divided by (n + 4).
items.s: The denominator grows without bound while the top stays fixed, so the members approach 0.

items.q: Find the limit of the list whose 2nd member is (3/4)^n.
items.s: The ratio 3/4 is less than one in size, so powers of it approach 0.

items.q: A continuous map takes the value -4 at one place and the value 4 at another. State the number whose existence between those two places is guaranteed by the intermediate value property.
items.s: A continuous map takes every value between -4 and 4, and zero lies between them, so a place where the output is 0 is guaranteed.

items.q: A continuous map on the closed stretch from 0 to 3 has its largest output equal to 4. State the largest output of the map on that stretch.
items.s: The extreme value property guarantees that the largest output is actually attained, and it is given as 4.

items.q: A continuous map on a closed stretch has outputs never below 2 and never above 3. State the smallest number you can guarantee is at least as large as every output of the map there.
items.s: Every output lies between 2 and 3, so 3 is at least as large as every output = 5.

items.q: Find the derivative of y = 2x^2 + 2x at x = 2 from the definition as a limit of a ratio of changes.
items.s: The difference quotient simplifies to 4x + 2 with a remainder that vanishes, so at x = 2 the value is 10.

items.q: Differentiate y = 1/x from first principles and state the value of the derivative at x = 4.
items.s: The difference quotient tends to minus 1 divided by x squared, so at x = 4 the value is -0.0625.

items.q: A map takes the value -1 at x = 5 and the value -3 at x = 10. Find the average slope over that stretch.
items.s: The average slope is the change in output divided by the change in input, that is (-3 - -1)/5 = -0.4.

items.q: For the map taking x to x^2 on the stretch from 0 to 3, split the stretch into 4 equal pieces and use the smallest output on each piece. Find the resulting lower total.
items.s: The smallest output on each piece is at its left end, and summing gives 5.91.

items.q: A stretch of length 3 is split into 4 equal pieces. State the mesh of that split.
items.s: The pieces all have width 3/4, and the mesh is the widest width, which is 0.75.

items.q: The 2nd member of a family of maps takes x to x/(n + 3). Find the value the outputs settle on at x = 4.
items.s: With x fixed the denominator grows without bound, so the outputs settle on 0.

items.q: Find the least counting number n for which n times 0.25 exceeds 1.
items.s: The inequality needs n greater than 1/0.25 = 4, so the least counting number that works is 5.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains continuity under uniform limits.
o: the fact that continuous maps whose outputs settle evenly have a continuous limit
the requirement that the maps eventually lie close to one another at every input at once
the largest gap between a map and a comparison map over the whole set
the stretch of inputs on which an endless total of powers settles to a finite value
items.s: continuity under uniform limits: the fact that continuous maps whose outputs settle evenly have a continuous limit. The other options describe uniform Cauchy condition, power series interval, supremum norm.

items.q: absolute value may be defined as
o: a part of the line that meets every open stretch of the line
the size of a number with any minus sign removed
the guarantee that every nonempty set bounded above has a least upper bound
the least of all the upper bounds of a set of numbers
items.s: absolute value: the size of a number with any minus sign removed. The other options describe dense subset, supremum, completeness property.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains continuous on a set.
o: the rule that sums, products and quotients of continuous functions are continuous where defined
a gap where the two sided approach value exists but differs from the value taken there
the property of being continuous at every member of that set
a gap where the two one sided approach values exist but are not equal
items.s: continuous on a set: the property of being continuous at every member of that set. The other options describe algebra of continuous functions, jump discontinuity, removable discontinuity.

items.q: “a list that possesses no such number” is the definition of
o: null sequence
convergent sequence
squeeze principle
divergent sequence

power series interval

Cauchy sequence
sequence
cluster point of a list

the rule that compares successive members of an endless total to decide whether the running totals settle
the property that the endless total of the sizes of the members is finite
the total obtained by adding the members of a list one after another
items.s: ratio test: the rule that compares successive members of an endless total to decide whether the running totals settle. The other options describe series, geometric series, absolute convergence.

the property that one closeness of inputs serves for every place in the set
the guarantee that a continuous function on a closed bounded stretch attains a largest and a smallest output
an input at which the output is zero
items.s: extreme value property: the guarantee that a continuous function on a closed bounded stretch attains a largest and a smallest output. The other options describe intermediate value property, root of an equation, uniform continuity.

the statement that a list trapped between two lists sharing one limit must share it too
a list that possesses no such number

a list that possesses a number its members eventually stay arbitrarily close to
